repeats.q:
Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
Figure 1 — top row: C Δ P; bottom row: F D R
Figure 2 — top row: F C Δ; bottom row: J R P
Figure 3 — top row: N C G; bottom row: T S H
Figure 4 — ?
o: Top row: T H G; bottom row: P N C
Top row: T N C; bottom row: P G H
Top row: T N C; bottom row: P H G
Top row: P N C; bottom row: T H G
repeats.e:
The six boxes form a ring; every symbol moves one place clockwise: top-left → top-middle → top-right → bottom-right → bottom-middle → bottom-left → top-left.
In figure 1 → 2: C, Δ move right, P drops to bottom-right, R moves to bottom-middle, F rises to top-left, and the letter landing at bottom-left is replaced by a new one.
Figure 3 → 4: top row T N C; bottom-right G, bottom-middle H, bottom-left a new letter.
Only the option with top T N C and bottom _ H G fits.
Answer: Top row: T N C; bottom row: P H G

repeats.q:
Eight symbol-number clusters are given below three of which are same. Find the three clusters that are exactly same.
(A) 74* &4%48@23*7^+#
(B) 74* &4%43@23*7$+#
(C) 74* &4%43@23*7^+#
(D) 74* &4%43@23*7^+#
(E) 74* &4$43@23*7^+#
(F) 74* &4%43@33*7^+#
(G) 74* &4&43@23*7^+#
(H) 74* &4%43@23*7^+#
repeats.e:
Take C (74* &4%43@23*7^+#) as reference.
A has 48, B has $ for ^, E has $ for %, F has 33 for 23, G has & for %.
D and H match C character for character.
Answer: C, D and H

repeats.q:
In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions. Find out which conclusion is true based on the given statement.
Statement: S = T < U ≤ V > W
Conclusions:
I. T < W
II. S < V
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
repeats.e:
I: T < U ≤ V > W — the sign flips at V, so T and W cannot be compared; I is false.
II: S = T < U ≤ V gives S < V; II is true.
Answer: Only II is true

repeats.q:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.
The scientist was known for her _________ adherence to ethical standards.
repeats.e:
The word is un + assail + able: double 's' once, single 'l' in assail, ending '-able'.
Correct spelling: unassailable (impossible to attack or question).
Answer: unassailable

repeats.q:
In this type of questions, question is provided with substitutes for various mathematical symbols, followed by a question involving calculation of an expression or choosing the correct/incorrect equation. You have to put the real signs in the given equation and then solve the questions as required.
If '*' stands for '+', '@' stands for '-', '%' stands for '×', '^' stands for '÷', then find the value of: 4 ^ 9 % 8 % 6 = ?
repeats.e:
After substitution: 4 ÷ 9 × 8 × 6.
Working left to right: 4/9 × 48 = 192/9.
192/9 reduces to 64/3.
Answer: 64/3

clock: Four sections, 15 minutes each, 25 questions each. The clock of a section stops when you submit it; you cannot go back.
Marks: +2 right, −0.5 wrong, 0 blank. Four wrong guesses cost one right answer, so a guess is worth it only when you have cut the options to two.
Order inside a section: do what you know first, mark the slow ones for review, come back with the time left. Never let one question eat 2 minutes.
Reasoning first by design: the 2026 papers put the fast marks here (coding, series, classification). Save the syllogism with three statements for the end of its 15 minutes.
Quant: mensuration, algebra and trigonometry are formula-first and quick; read DI tables once, write the totals on the rough sheet; leave geometry constructions for last.
English: do spelling, idioms, one-word, synonyms and antonyms first (10 marks in 3 minutes), then narration and voice, then error spotting, then the passage or cloze with the time left.
GA: 25 questions in 15 minutes is generous. Answer what you know, skip what you do not: a GA guess without eliminating two options is a losing bet.
night: Read this sheet once tonight and once in the morning. Nothing new tonight: no new topic, no new book.
Admit card, photo ID, the pen, and the centre route checked tonight. Reach 45 minutes early.
Sleep 7 hours. A tired brain misreads 'not' in syllogisms and signs in series.
hall: Rough sheet: draw the alphabet strip (A1 to Z26, EJOTY at 5 10 15 20 25) and the family-tree symbols before the clock starts on Reasoning.
Read every question stem to the end. 2026 papers hid the trick in the last line: 'not', 'except', 'wrongly spelt', 'does NOT follow'.
Statement questions in GA: judge each statement on its own, then pick the option. Two true statements and a 'both' option is the 2026 pattern.
Last two minutes of each section: answer every question where you have narrowed to two options; leave the rest blank; press Submit yourself.
